ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. Proto-Germanic *anda- Proto-Indo-European *swer-der. Proto-Germanic *swarō Proto-Germanic *andaswarō Proto-West Germanic *andaswaru Old English andswaru Middle English answere English answer From Middle English answere, andsware, from Old English andswaru (“answer”), from and- (“against”) + swaru (“affirmation”), (from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ent- (“front, forehead”) and Old English swerian (“to swear”), from Proto-Indo-European *swer-), suggesting an original meaning of "a sworn statement rebutting a charge".

Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntsder. Proto-Germanic *anda- Proto-Indo-European *swer-der. Proto-Germanic *swarjaną Proto-Germanic *andaswarjaną Old English andswerian Middle English answeren English answer From Middle English answeren, andswaren, answerien, from Old English andswarian, answarien (“to answer, to respond, to deny an allegation under oath”), from Proto-Germanic *andaswarōną, *andaswarjaną (“to answer, to give a response, to rebut”), from *anda- (“against”) + *swarjaną, *swarōną (“to swear an oath, to answer, to respond”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ent- (“face, forehead”) and *swer-…

senses.d: A response or reply; something said or done in reaction to a statement or question.
ex: Her answer to his proposal was a slap in the face.
There is no simple answer to corruption.
Violence is not the answer to disagreements.

senses.d: Someone or something that fills a similar role or position.
A document filed in response to a complaint, responding to each point raised in the complaint and raising counterpoints.
To make a reply or response to.
ex: She answers him as if she knew his mind:

senses.d: To speak in defence against; to reply to in defence.
ex: to answer a charge or accusation

senses.d: To respond to a call by someone at a door or telephone, or other similar piece of equipment.
ex: Nobody answered when I knocked on the door.

senses.d: To suit a need or purpose satisfactorily.
To be accountable or responsible; to make amends.
ex: The man must answer to his employer for the money entrusted to his care.
He has a lot to answer for.

senses.d: To file a document in response to a complaint.
To correspond to; to be in harmony with; to be in agreement with.
ex:
1775, Richard Brinsley Sheridan, The Duenna, Dublin: G. Burnet et al., 1794, Act II, Scene 2, p. 25,
Egad, I wish she had answer’d her picture as well.
The use of dunder in the making of rum, answers the purpose of yeast in the fermentation of flour.

senses.d: To be opposite, or to act in opposition.
ex: The windows answering each other, we could just discern the glowing horizon through them […]

senses.d: To be or act in conformity, or by way of accommodation, correspondence, relation, or proportion; to conform; to correspond; to suit; usually with to.
ex: […] that the time may haue all ſhadow, and ſilence in it: and the place anſwere to conuenience
If this but answer to my just belief, / I’ll well remember you.

senses.d: To respond to satisfactorily; to meet successfully by way of explanation, argument, or justification; to refute.
ex: […] no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.
The reasoning was not and could not be answered.

ety.text: From the feminine of répons, or from Old French response, from respons (also the past participle of respondre), a semi-learned word from Latin respōnsum. Cf. the verb répondre.
From rispondere, corrupted by posta, feminine past participle of porre. Compare Asturian and Spanish respuesta; Catalan, Galician, and Portuguese resposta.
From responder, corrupted by puesta, feminine past participle of poner. Compare Asturian respuesta, Catalan, Galician, and Portuguese resposta, Italian risposta.

From Old Galician-Portuguese resposta, reposta, from responder, corrupted by posta, feminine past participle of põer (Portuguese pôr). Compare Asturian and Spanish respuesta, Catalan and Galician resposta and Italian risposta.
From Latin contestātiōnem. By surface analysis, contestar + -ción.

chain.g: The act of loosening or unfastening someone or something; dissolution.

ety.text: Inherited from Old French solucion, from Latin solūtiōnem, from the verb solvō.
Deverbal from replicar (“to replicate”), from Latin replicāre (“to fold”), from re- + plicō (“to fold”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleḱ- (“to plait, to weave”).
Inherited from Middle French respondre, from Old French respondre, from Late Latin respondere, from Latin respondēre.

it:rispondere.gl: to answer, to reply, to respond [with a ‘to’]

ety.text: From Late Latin respondere, from Latin respondēre.

Inherited from Old Spanish responder, inherited from Latin respondēre (likely via Late Latin respondĕre). The original past participle was respuso or repuso in Old Spanish. The expected diphthongization of stressed Latin /ŏ/ is found in Asturian responder (that is, respuendo) and sporadically in Old Spanish as well.
Borrowed from Latin contestārī (“to call to witness”).

pt:responder.gl: to answer; to reply (to give a written or spoken response)

senses.d: The act of giving an answer.
ex: An answer that comes out of the whirlwind is, logically, no answer at all: it belongs to a world above that of logical answerings.
